message.content:
Research these questions about the memos codebase at /bench/repo. Give me detailed findings with exact file paths and line numbers.

**h14**: Each memo carries derived metadata computed from its content rather than set by the user (used for lists/previews). Where is it computed, which operations trigger recomputation, and what does the computation extract?

Look at:
- /bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/ for memo payload computation
- /bench/repo/store/memo.go for the memo data structure
- grep for "payload" or "snippet" or "property" in server/ and store/
- Check what fields are computed from content (e.g., snippet, tags, links, etc.)

**h15**: Memo visibility (who may view a memo) is enforced in more than one server surface. List every distinct enforcement site (there are at least three) with files.

Look at:
- grep for "visibility" or "Visibility" across server/ files
- Check all RPC handlers and HTTP handlers that serve memos
- Look for access control checks related to memo visibility
- Check RSS, API, and other surfaces

Read all relevant files and report exact function names, paths, and line numbers.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

121		list, err := s.ListMemos(ctx, find)
122		if err != nil {
123			return nil, err
124		}
125		if len(list) == 0 {
126			return nil, nil
127		}

129		memo := list[0]
130		return memo, nil

134		if update.UID != nil && !base.UIDMatcher.MatchString(*update.UID) {
135			return errors.New("invalid uid")
136		}
137		return s.driver.UpdateMemo(ctx, update)

140	func (s *Store) DeleteMemo(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteMemo) error {
141		// Clean up memo_relation records where this memo is either the source or target.
142		if err := s.driver.DeleteMemoRelation(ctx, &DeleteMemoRelation{MemoID: &delete.ID}); err != nil {
143			return err
144		}
145		if err := s.driver.DeleteMemoRelation(ctx, &DeleteMemoRelation{RelatedMemoID: &delete.ID}); err != nil {
146			return err
147		}
148		// Clean up attachments linked to this memo.
149		attachments, err := s.ListAttachments(ctx, &FindAttachment{MemoID: &delete.ID})
150		if err != nil {
151			return err
152		}
153		for _, attachment := range attachments {
154			if err := s.DeleteAttachment(ctx, &DeleteAttachment{ID: attachment.ID}); err != nil {
155				return err
156			}
157		}
158		return s.driver.DeleteMemo(ctx, delete)
159	}

## H14: Derived Metadata (Memo Payload) Computation

### Where it is computed

The core computation happens in `RebuildMemoPayload` at `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, lines 74-87. This function delegates to `markdownService.ExtractAll()`, which is implemented at `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 355-422.

The `ExtractAll` function parses the memo's markdown content using goldmark into an AST, then walks the AST in a single pass to extract all metadata.

### What the computation extracts

The derived metadata is stored in a `MemoPayload` protobuf, defined at `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto`, lines 7-29:

1. **`tags`** (repeated string) -- All `#tag` nodes found in the markdown, deduplicated while preserving case. Extracted by walking AST for `TagNode` instances (markdown.go line 377).

2. **`property`** (a `MemoPayload_Property` sub-message) containing:
   - **`has_link`** (bool) -- Set to true if any `gast.KindLink` node exists (line 393-394).
   - **`has_task_list`** (bool) -- Set to true if any GFM `TaskCheckBox` node exists (line 399-400).
   - **`has_code`** (bool) -- Set to true if any `CodeBlock`, `FencedCodeBlock`, or `CodeSpan` node exists (lines 396-397).
   - **`has_incomplete_tasks`** (bool) -- Set to true if any unchecked `TaskCheckBox` exists (lines 401-404).
   - **`title`** (string) -- Extracted from the first block-level child of the document if it is an H1 heading (lines 383-388).

3. **`mentions`** ([]string, in the `ExtractedData` struct but not stored in the proto payload directly) -- `@mention` usernames found in the content (line 379-380). These are used at ingestion time for notification dispatch but are not persisted in the payload.

Additionally, a **`snippet`** (plain text summary, max 64 chars) is computed on-the-fly each time a memo is converted for API responses. This is NOT stored in the payload but computed at read time by `getMemoContentSnippet` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, lines 83-89, which calls `markdownService.GenerateSnippet()` at `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`, lines 263-346. The snippet strips markdown formatting, skips code blocks, and truncates at a word boundary.

The payload also has a **`location`** field, but this is user-set (not derived from content).

### Which operations trigger recomputation

Three triggers:

1. **CreateMemo** -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 108:
   ```go
   if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
   ```

2. **UpdateMemo** (when `content` field is in the update mask) -- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 447:
   ```go
   if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
   ```

3. **Runner.RunOnce** (batch rebuild of all memos) -- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, lines 27-71. This iterates over all memos in batches of 100, calling `RebuildMemoPayload` for each, then persisting via `Store.UpdateMemo`. Note: this batch runner is NOT currently wired into server startup (unlike the S3 presign runner); it exists as an available operation but has no automatic trigger in `server.go`.

### How derived metadata is served to clients

In `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 47-80:
- `memo.Payload.Tags` is mapped to `memoMessage.Tags` (line 48)
- `memo.Payload.Property` is converted via `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` to `memoMessage.Property` (line 49, defined at lines 315-326)
- `snippet` is computed live from `memo.Content` and set on `memoMessage.Snippet` (lines 76-80)

## H15: Memo Visibility Enforcement Sites

Visibility has three levels: `PUBLIC` (anyone), `PROTECTED` (any authenticated user), `PRIVATE` (creator only, plus admins in some surfaces). Enforcement occurs in at least **nine distinct sites** across different server surfaces:

### 1. `checkMemoReadAccess` -- Central gRPC memo access guard
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 39-68

The primary enforcement function. Checks:
- Archived memos: only visible to their creator (lines 45-53)
- Non-public memos: requires authentication (line 60); PRIVATE memos require creator match (line 63)

Called from:
- `GetMemo` (line 356)
- `GetMemo` for parent memo (line 367)
- `ListMemoComments` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` (line 148)

### 2. `ListMemos` -- Query-level visibility filtering
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 218-227

Applies `VisibilityList` and filter constraints at the database query level:
- Anonymous users: only `PUBLIC` memos (line 219)
- Authenticated users viewing others' memos: `PUBLIC` + `PROTECTED` (line 225)
- Authenticated users viewing their own: no visibility restriction

### 3. RSS feed service -- Public-only filtering
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`
- System RSS (`GetSystemRSS`): line 90 -- `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}`
- User RSS (`GetUserRSS`): line 141 -- `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}`

Both feeds only serve PUBLIC memos.

### 4. Frontend sitemap -- Public-only filtering
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`, line 150

`VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` -- Only public memos appear in the XML sitemap.

### 5. File server (attachment access) -- Visibility-based file serving
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, lines 666-704

Checks memo visibility when serving attachment files:
- PUBLIC memo + anonymous access allowed: serve without auth (line 677)
- Share token fallback for any visibility (lines 684-688)
- PRIVATE memo: only creator or admin (line 699)

### 6. Reaction service -- Inline visibility checks
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`
- `ListMemoReactions`: lines 29-41 -- Non-public requires auth; PRIVATE requires creator or super-user
- `UpsertMemoReaction`: lines 82-85 -- PRIVATE requires creator or super-user

### 7. Attachment service (gRPC) -- Visibility via linked memo
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`, lines 422-455 (`checkAttachmentAccess`)

For attachments linked to a memo, access follows the memo's visibility:
- PUBLIC: open access (line 445)
- PRIVATE: creator or super-user only (line 451)

### 8. SSE hub -- Visibility-based event delivery filtering
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`, lines 134-143 (`canReceive`)

Server-Sent Events are filtered per client:
- PRIVATE events: only delivered to the creator or admin users (line 137)
- PUBLIC/PROTECTED/"": delivered to all connected clients (line 138)

### 9. User notifications -- Visibility-gated notification payloads
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go`, lines 302-316 (`canViewerAccessMemo`)

When converting inbox notifications to API responses, checks whether the viewer can see the referenced memos:
- Admin bypasses (line 306)
- PRIVATE: only if viewer is the creator (line 309-310)
- PROTECTED: only if viewer is authenticated (line 312-313)

Used at lines 337, 342 (comment notifications) and line 370, 385 (mention notifications) to suppress notification payloads for inaccessible memos.

### 10. Notification email delivery -- Visibility check
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go`, lines 306-320 (`canViewerAccessMemo`)

A separate (duplicated) implementation of the same visibility logic for email notification rendering:
- PRIVATE: viewer must be the creator (line 313-314)
- PROTECTED: viewer must exist (line 316-317)

### 11. User stats service -- Query-level visibility filtering
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`
- `ListAllUserStats`: lines 84-91 -- Anonymous gets PUBLIC only; other-user gets PUBLIC+PROTECTED
- `GetUserStats`: lines 217-221 -- Same pattern

### 12. Memo relation service and batch relation converter -- Visibility-filtered relation queries
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`, lines 107-112
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 182-187

Both construct a `memoFilter` string based on the current user:
- Anonymous: `visibility == "PUBLIC"` 
- Authenticated: `creator_id == {id} || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`

This filter is passed to `ListMemoRelations` to prevent leaking related memos that the viewer cannot access.

### 13. Mention notification helpers -- Visibility check
**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go`, lines 56-72 (`canUserAccessMentionContext`)

Checks both the memo and its related memo:
- PRIVATE memos: only accessible if the target user is the creator (lines 62-63, 67-68)

Used by `shouldSkipMentionInbox` (line 88) to suppress mention notifications for memos the target cannot see.
